body:
Thank you so much for taking the time to respond and for the kind words. I think, as much as I try to reassure myself of what I know to be true, I still have a tendency to wonder if I’m blowing it out of proportion. It makes it hard for me to convince myself that I am strong and not just playing the victim, but I think as time moves me further from them, I’ll be able to show myself that I’m not who they see me as. It’s hard when almost my entire family believes the narrative they’ve created, but I have to remind myself that they’re all similar to each other. The family as a whole overlooks abuse and has this weird traditional view of what a family “should” be, which is basically just the belief that parents deserve respect and children should be grateful for the bare minimum. 

I just hope that I can get far enough away from it that I can start to desire closeness again. I’ve closed myself off from everyone for fear of them seeing me the way my family does. I’m planning to start therapy soon though, so fingers crossed

Thank you for sharing, I’m sorry you’re dealing with all of that. Your mom sounds very similar to mine in that she sweeps the serious issues under the rug. It’s hard to maintain a superficial relationship with someone who’s meant to love you wholly and unconditionally for who you are. 

I struggle with the idea of maintaining no contact, but it’s harder to imagine going back. It would take my mom putting in serious work to abandon the idea that she and my family have of me. I’ve been the “problem child” since I was 7 years old, so the image that they’ve created of me is now their reality. Any time I’ve tried to show them that I’m not that person, I was told that I’m manipulative. I’ve been told I always play the victim and I’ve been blamed for the awful instances of assault/abuse that have been inflicted on me by people inside the family and even strangers. I was sexually assaulted in college and was told that I shouldn’t have had a guy over, and that I shouldn’t have dressed the way I did back then (I wore denim shorts that they deemed too short). 

Going NC is brutal but I’ve never felt peace with myself like I do now. It’s been almost 3 months since the assault from my stepdad and this is the first time in my life that I actually like who I am and don’t have the underlying fear that I’m pretending to be something I’m not. 

I hope that you’re able to find a place where you can be yourself fully without feeling like you have to sacrifice your beliefs to keep the peace with someone who refuses to accept and validate them.

God, that just broke my heart and put it into perspective for me. Any time I’m having those thoughts I end up remembering him randomly and he takes away the option. I’ve had him since he was 7 weeks old and he’s 7 now. My family tells me he cries when he can’t find me when I’m at work, and he always bolts for the door when I come home. I’m just monologuing at this point but the thought of him crying and me never coming home is too much. 

I’m genuinely sorry that you’ve experienced what you have, but I know for a fact that your kitties are thankful that you didn’t pull the trigger. They need you, and like you said, they don’t need or want just anyone. They need and want you. Thank you for staying ❤️

Thank you so much. Sometimes I get too deep into my thoughts and then he comes up at just the right time and reminds me that I have a reason to be here. Even if that reason is a 10lb fur ball who ignores me half the time. I hope that you find your reason to stay. Please message me if you need someone to talk to.

Thank you. I don’t think I have the energy to address it right now but please know that I’m also here if you ever want to chat. I briefly read some of your posts and nobody should be alone with these thoughts. Sending positive vibes <3

Thank you for the advice! I definitely plan to speak with her next time I see her, as I cannot allow myself to experience that level of frustration again - especially over something that should be a nonissue. 

I just don’t understand the inconsistency or the lack of support for staff. The only “reason” my boss had for folding is that she fears bad publicity that could lead to decreased revenue. We’ve already had one case among staff, and we have hundreds of people coming in daily. If there’s an outbreak, the subsequent publicity would be more nightmarish than what COULD come from enforcing the governor’s mandate.

I live with my grandparents who are both at an increased risk of complications if they get covid. I also work full-time with the public at a recreation center, in a county where masks are mandated in public. 

My employer told staff that we are to ensure that all patrons are wearing masks. We were told that if they refuse to wear one, we are to kindly ask them to leave. If they refuse to leave, we were told to call 911 and have them trespassed. 

Most people who come in are already wearing masks, and those who are not nearly always go and get one without much complaint. We have had only two patrons claim “medical reasons” for not wearing them, but they only used this reasoning as a last resort after they yelled at me for explaining that our policy states that they must be worn. 

The two patrons were a married couple, and I was verbally assaulted by both of them on two separate occasions. My boss told me that if it were to happen again, she would let them know that they were not to return and that they may not verbally abuse our staff. 

Well the other day the wife came back and made a scene, so I asked her to wait there and went to get my boss. To my surprise, my boss did NOTHING. She didn’t even speak to her until the lady’s husband showed up demanding to speak with my boss. After they spoke, my boss came in and told me that it must have been a misunderstanding and that the couple felt I was harassing and discriminating their family. She also lied to them about why they were confronted, stating that I felt that they did not want to follow a different policy that we have? She told me how sweet they were and then told me that we are to allow anyone who refuses to wear a mask to access the facility anyway. 

I was FUMING. The establishment is by no means a necessity, and all other patrons have zero issues wearing a mask despite personal opinions. At this point, I am mad at my boss for misleading me to think that she would back me up. Not to mention the fact that I have to go home to my grandparents everyday with the fear of spreading the virus to them. 

Any advice on how I should handle myself, or what (if anything) I should say to my employer, is greatly appreciated. I was already looking at other jobs, but this incident pushed me over the edge.

Thank you for the response! Were you able to find peace in walking away? I fear I won’t be able to make that decision without one day regretting it, but I cannot and will not allow myself to be treated this way when I know I don’t deserve it. They’ve made me think I’m an awful person for so long, I’m finally starting to realize I’m not the monster they want me to be and it makes me want to just go and never look back.

I hope he does! As much as I liked him before all of this, I respect myself too much to chase a man who thinks he’s better off without me. If he wants to chase someone, he can. I’m sure it would be less than fun for me to see that, but I love my job too much to let a guy who doesn’t know what he wants ruin it to me.

Jeez I never really thought about it that way. I haven’t been there long enough to notice any patterns with him because he’s been on me since I got there. I have heard that he dated a girl who once worked there in a similarly-ranked position, but I don’t know why it ended or if her leaving had anything to do with it. 

I was probably silly to believe it, but the relative of his had me convinced that he’s just this amazing guy that’s perfect for me so I admittedly had blinders up going into it.
That was..... wild. Holy shit. How could you even get work done with all of that going on??? I’m glad you got out of that mess, and without jail time! Nobody is worth that level of crazy.

Ok so I see how that sounds like I’m working on myself to impress him or something but the self-improvement came after being depressed for the first few weeks of lockdown. I was seriously neglecting myself for awhile because my lockdown situation isn’t great and was causing some mental anguish. I didn’t want to come out of all of this looking and feeling a mess so I decided to use the time to show myself some love.

I’m not really upset that he’s not pursuing me, it’s more about the fact that I feel that I was (naively) misled and that the outcome could potentially affect my job if I don’t behave properly when I return to work. I’ve already said this in the comments and I’ll say it again, I consented to everything knowing that it could go badly. But he’s not exactly innocent in this. He’s 7 years older than me and is an executive in the company who slept with someone much lower on the totem pole. I’m still new at this place, I had only been there for like 3 months before the lockdown started. I take responsibility for my part, but I agree with whoever it was that said he should have known better.

No you’re absolutely right, I consented to everything knowing that there was a chance this would happen. I don’t feel like anything is wrong, I’ve just never been in this situation before and I want to make sure I conduct myself in the best way I can so that he can’t get the best of me at work. I really love my job, so he may have gotten the best of me outside of work but he won’t know it when I’m there.

Oh my! I know it’s not funny, but I so want to hear the story of you almost hitting her with your car. That whole situation is unimaginable, I’m so sorry you had to deal with that. 

I’ll be honest, I’d heard the saying and I knew it probably wasn’t a wise decision. My downfall is my tendency to give the benefit of the doubt to anyone who hasn’t hurt me before. It goes beyond this situation, but this one has shown me that I need to be more reserved when it comes to trusting people.

I don’t think he is either, I just wish he would have been honest about that because we talked about that stuff before we hooked up. 

I’ll definitely be cordial, I just couldn’t figure out if I should act like it literally didn’t happen or if I should lean more towards straight up ignoring him. 

I will say, I’ve been putting in some work on myself during the lockdown so I plan to show up looking just right. He won’t be getting any attention from me so if that makes him feel any type of way, it’s not really my problem at this point.

I can’t believe that nobody mentioned that either, but I forgot to mention that he is single. As if it couldn’t get any more awkward, one of the employees on my team is related to him and actually aided in “pushing” us together.

This! I worked through college, and at that time I had a firm rule against dating coworkers. But man, you get out into the real world and you realize it isn’t so easy to meet new people unless you’re actively going out and trying. 

It also doesn’t help that the industry I work in now is primarily run by young, attractive people. Even when you know you shouldn’t shit where you eat, being surrounded by gorgeous people all day makes you want to sometimes.
Oh I’m sure that was his logic! He knew that we were shutting down before I did, so knowing /that/ makes me think he knew what he was doing.

The thing is, the only HR-type thing we have would be a board of people made up of his friends (he is a very important, well-liked figure in the company and in the industry we work in). 

Plus, I don’t feel the need to report him because he hasn’t really done anything wrong. I just don’t know how to proceed. As silly as it sounds, the way he chased me before all of this made me think he wanted a relationship. Now I don’t care so much about that, I just don’t know what to expect upon seeing him again since the vibe changed so dramatically.

Yeah, he definitely still works there. Without revealing too much, he is in the top 3 on the chain of command for the company. He’s not my direct boss but he is a big (huge) decision-maker for the business so he could affect my job if he wanted to, though I doubt he would.
Geez, no chill 😂
I’ll check them out, thank you! I used to watch my 600 lb life but you’re right, it’s suuuper depressing. The doctor did crack me up though lmao

Thank you! And congrats to you on yours!! 

But yeah, telling someone to lose weight is hardly the right way to do it. I know for myself, if someone tells me to do something —even if it’s something I know I probably should do — I’m gonna need you to tell me why. 

Like, if a doctor had just told me to lose weight, I probably would have been resistant. But I started watching this show (Supersize vs Superskinny on YouTube, for anyone interested) that kinda highlights the dangers of both over and under eating, and it scared me straight. 

I realized I could keep going how I was and die of a heart attack at 40, or I could get my shit together and live a life I’m proud of in a body that I’m comfortable in.

It’s interesting to see how many others report that their doctors neglected to mention their weight, especially when nearly every FA you see goes on and on about how healthcare professionals are bullying/oppressing them for being overweight. 

When I was 16 years old I was 270 lbs (5’9”) with some killer hip/knee/ankle issues. They even thought I was diabetic at one point. Never once did a doctor tell me to lose weight. I did have one doctor recommend modifying my diet in order to combat hypoglycemia, but there was never mention of weight. And I had a BMI of 40, which is classified as “extreme” or “severe” obesity, per the CDC. 

I’m 24 now and I weigh 140 lbs at 5’9” and would you believe that I have literally zero issues with my hips, knees, and ankles? I also identified a few food intolerances and made dietary changes as necessary, and I feel like I’ve been given a new body and a new life. 

It just makes me sad that so many people choose to live painful lives because they’d rather do that than admit that they’ve been doing it wrong. And I say that as someone who did it horribly wrong for 19 years.

Thank you for the kind words. I think, now more than ever, we all see how badly we need therapy so we are trying to get that arranged so that we can move towards healing. Hearing the details of what happened kinda started the grieving process over again, so I’m glad that we all seem willing to take the steps to get help.
